transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. To start, can you tell me when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise, including gardening, after 1 week. Please avoid heavy work for a month.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise. If you’re running out, your GP should be able to provide more.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thank you. I'm also very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Mild light sensitivity can be normal as your eyes adjust, and wearing sunglasses outside can help. But significant pain in bright light, or severe light sensitivity, especially with a red and painful eye, is not normal and may need checking.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It’s common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after your operation. It should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I have for now. Thank you so much for the information.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help!
